summary: Backend-only regression + Convex write-through bridge verification after the 4-domain migration (routes / vouchers / purchases / notifications + agent map). 20/20 new tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration10_convex_bridge.py covering: FastAPI endpoint regression (health auth products vouchers routes notifications tracking) + mirror verification for every write-through path (purchases POST, deliveries POST notify, routes save/optimize/stop-status/delete, locations POST, user last_location) + Convex role gates (STAFF-only routes:list / purchases:list / tracking:agents, AGENT-only routes:mine, bad-token errors) + bridge fire-and-forget resiliency. Convex functions correctly refuse FIELD_AGENT and bad tokens. The bridge mirrors specific ids within <12s on every mutation and `cx_delete` correctly removes the route from Convex. No existing FastAPI endpoint was broken by the bridge edits.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/convex_bridge.py is tight and correct: `_run` swallows every exception, HTTP code != 200 or `status != success` is just logged, so a Convex outage can never 500 a FastAPI endpoint. Verified empirically — all mirrored endpoints return 200 even while Convex is being hammered.

frontend/convex/bridge.ts uses the shared SECRET constant inline (also in backend/.env CONVEX_BRIDGE_SECRET + hardcoded fallback in convex_bridge.py). Not a blocker, but worth centralising later via a Convex env var (`process.env.CONVEX_BRIDGE_SECRET` + `ctx.env`) so the rotation is one-step.

convex/routes.ts::save strips _id/_creationTime correctly via cleanRoute, but it inserts the new doc directly (not via upsert) — would duplicate rows if the FastAPI bridge mirror races ahead; in practice fine because the FastAPI route creates the mongo doc first, mirrors with bridge:upsert on `id`, and Convex save mutation is only called from the Convex path (not currently wired to the app). No action needed.
convex/routes.ts::kpis does a `by_distributor` query per route inside a loop — O(routes*sales) read; fine at test size, flag for scale.

success_rate.backend: 100% — 20/20 new bridge tests pass in isolation; mirrored FastAPI endpoints all 200 and documents land in Convex within polling window
success_rate.frontend: skipped — Google OAuth login cannot be automated per request

seed_data_creation: Ran /app/backend/seed_test.py (idempotent). Module-scoped fixture then syncs each seeded token into Convex via auth:syncSession so Convex functions can resolve the bearer token. Test data is prefixed TEST_ (products / suppliers / notes) and the test route is deleted at the end of the routes test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To exercise Convex functions you MUST first POST auth:syncSession for each token via https://fearless-ostrich-878.eu-west-1.convex.cloud/api/mutation — the test file does this automatically in a module-scoped autouse fixture. Convex has TWO HTTP endpoints: /api/mutation (bridge:*, auth:*, notifications:readAll, routes:save/optimize/stopStatus/remove) and /api/query (purchases:list, routes:list/mine/kpis, vouchers:list, notifications:list, tracking:agents). IMPORTANT shape gotchas: notifications:list returns {items:[], unread:N}, not a bare array. Convex writes are mirrored by FastAPI with cx_upsert/cx_insert/cx_delete which are fire-and-forget — always poll (wait_for_cx helper) rather than asserting immediately. Running the full /app/backend/tests/ suite exposes PRE-EXISTING ordering bugs in test_iteration2.TestUpgradeRequests and test_iteration7.TestC_PaymentVouchers (shared module-level STATE dict assumes earlier tests ran) — these are unrelated to the Convex bridge, see the serial run that still shows the same 5 state-dependent failures without my new file.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bug found. Full green on the bridge tests. The pre-existing full-suite failures in test_iteration2 (TestUpgradeRequests: 6 failures all KeyError 'plan_id'/'req_id') and test_iteration7 (TestC_PaymentVouchers: 8 failures all KeyError 'c1') are classic 'test depends on module-level STATE populated by an earlier test running first' problems that surface the moment pytest-xdist loadscope splits the module or the earlier test gets filtered out. They reproduce IDENTICALLY without the iteration10 file in the collection, so they are not a Convex-bridge regression.
